answer: Club rosters offer a costlier signal when a dues-paying society, say a river rowing crew or walnut growers' cooperative, signs one token per member-year and may sponsor at most 2% of its roll. Fake heads therefore need a real membership each, and the quota forces large rings to buy into ever more clubs. Sampled audits, such as asking a member to recite the club's latest sonnet night minutes, revoke a lying club's signing key.
